title: Syntara Plugin SDK - Common Definitions
description: Shared reusable definitions for the Syntara Automation Orchestrator Plugin SDK. These components are referenced across all step types to ensure strict backwards compatibility and consistent runtime behavior.

StepTypeManifest.title: Step Type Manifest (K8s CRD Structure)
StepTypeManifest.description: Top-level schema for step type manifests following Kubernetes Custom Resource Definition conventions. All manifests must declare apiVersion, kind, metadata, and spec sections.

apiVersion.description: API version following Kubernetes conventions. Must be 'syntara.io/v1alpha1'.

metadata.description: Step metadata for identification, versioning, and UI discovery.

name.description: Internal step identifier (snake_case). Used as the primary key for lookups.

namespace.description: Namespace identifier grouping this step under its owning domain or vendor (R3/AC-2). Combined with name it forms the globally unique step identity, and the canvas uses it to group the palette.

displayName.description: Human-readable step name displayed in the UI palette and canvas.

version.description: Semantic version of this step type.

description.description: Multi-line description of the step's purpose and capabilities.

tags.description: User-defined tags for organization and filtering.

documentationUrl.description: Optional link to the step's detailed documentation.

spec.description: Step specification defining category, execution, inputs, outputs, and requirements.

image.description: Runtime environment the execution plane runs the step in. It holds an interpreter and the SDK, not step code -- the step implementations live in the plugin artifact. Usually a generic runner reused across steps and plugins; a step with unusual dependencies may warrant its own. Null when the step requires no runtime image.

entrypoint.description: Step handle in 'module.path:ClassName' form, resolving to this step's BaseStep subclass within the plugin artifact. A plugin may package several steps (R8), so the runtime needs this to know which one to load and invoke through the SDK base class. This is not a shell command: running the step as a subprocess would bypass the base-class input validation and redaction checks. Null when the runtime needs no handle.

declaredRequirements.description: Declared capability, credential, and platform requirements.

capabilities.description: Required security clearance tags and capabilities.

credentialTypes.description: Types of credentials this step can consume.

outputs.description: Output schema defining what the step returns.

retryPolicy.description: Automatic retry configuration for transient failures.

StandardOutputWrapper.title: Standard Output Wrapper
StandardOutputWrapper.description: Mandatory, backwards-compatible output envelope for all task executions. This standardized structure enables workflow template expressions like ${fetch_data.Result.stdout} to remain stable across step versions. The backend scheduler and frontend canvas depend on this exact structure.

Result.description: Primary task return payload. Type varies by step implementation - may be an object (e.g., {stdout, stderr, exit_code}), string, array, or null. This is the data referenced in downstream workflow template expressions.

StatusCode.description: Numeric execution status following POSIX exit code conventions. 0 indicates success. Non-zero values indicate failure states. The execution plane and workflow engine use this status for their respective execution and workflow decisions.

StatusMessage.description: Human-readable execution summary displayed in the UI execution history timeline. Should be concise (recommended max 200 characters) and describe what the task accomplished or attempted.

ErrorMessage.description: Detailed error diagnostics populated only on failure (StatusCode > 0). Should include stack traces, validation errors, or API error responses to aid debugging. Credential redaction and persistence are execution-plane responsibilities.

DependencyDeclaration.title: Dependency Declaration
DependencyDeclaration.description: Declarative version constraints and capability requirements for step execution. The platform validates these at workflow deployment time (not runtime) to prevent dependency hell and version conflicts. Failure to satisfy dependencies blocks workflow execution.

platformVersion.description: SemVer-compatible version range specifying the minimum required Syntara platform engine version. Examples: '>=3.0.0', '^3.1.0', '3.x'. The scheduler rejects steps requiring newer platform capabilities than the deployed version.

capabilities.description: Standardized capability and security requirement tags used for administrative review and execution-plane policy matching. These declarations express what the step needs; they do not grant access or define the enforcement implementation. Filesystem-related tags include 'readonly-root-filesystem' and 'tmpfs-mount'.

collections.description: Version-bounded Ansible collection dependencies required by the step. The platform uses these declarations to validate and construct a compatible execution environment; the provisioning implementation is execution-plane-owned.

name.description: Fully-qualified Ansible Galaxy collection name in namespace.collection format.

version.description: SemVer version constraint for the collection.

extensions.description: Required peer extension dependencies (other Community Step Packages). The platform validates these are installed and version-compatible before allowing workflow deployment. Used when one step builds on another's functionality.

name.description: Package name of the required extension, following npm scoping conventions for Community Steps.

version.description: SemVer version constraint for the extension.

ResourceRequirements.title: Resource Requirements
ResourceRequirements.description: CPU and memory allocation boundaries supplied to the execution plane for resource validation and enforcement. These constraints help prevent runaway tasks from starving platform resources and enable accurate cost accounting; the SDK does not select the worker or provisioning backend.

limits.description: Maximum resource ceiling supplied to the execution plane. Setting limits too low can cause task failures; setting them too high can waste platform capacity.

cpu.description: CPU limit in Kubernetes quantity format. Integer values = cores (e.g., '2' = 2 cores). Decimal/suffix = millicores (e.g., '500m' = 0.5 cores). Typical range: 100m-4.

memory.description: Memory limit in Kubernetes quantity format. Supports Ki, Mi, Gi suffixes (binary, base-1024). Typical range: 128Mi-8Gi.

requests.description: Minimum resource reservation supplied to the execution plane. Setting requests equal to limits expresses a predictable resource boundary; setting requests below limits permits platform-specific overcommitment.

cpu.description: CPU request in Kubernetes quantity format. Should typically match limits for compute-intensive tasks to avoid throttling.

memory.description: Memory request in Kubernetes quantity format. It should typically be 80–100% of the limit to balance predictable capacity with controlled bursting.

ExecutionTimeout.title: Execution Timeout
ExecutionTimeout.description: Maximum task execution duration in seconds, supplied to the execution plane for timeout enforcement. Prevents hung tasks from blocking workflow completion. Minimum 1 second, maximum 24 hours (86400 seconds).

SchedulingControls.title: Scheduling Controls
SchedulingControls.description: Developer-declared scheduling controls for placement and connectivity. These controls may be used for validation and review, but they are not the effective sandbox, egress, or worker-pool policy; Syntara registration settings are authoritative.

affinity_labels.description: Developer-declared step-affinity controls. Each label is a key=value pair (or key-only). The administrative worker_pool_selector supplied during registration is authoritative for pool selection.

connectivity_requirements.description: Developer-declared connectivity controls used for validation and administrative review. Each entry is either a bare destination string or an object pairing a destination with explicit port/protocol specifications. The effective egress mode is the administrative egress_policy from step registration, not a developer manifest value.

oneOf.description: Destination hostname, FQDN, IPv4 address, or IPv4 CIDR block. Egress is permitted on all ports unless narrowed via the object form.
A destination paired with explicit port/protocol specifications for administrative review and execution-plane connectivity policy matching.

host.description: Target hostname, FQDN, IPv4 address, or IPv4 CIDR block.

ports.description: Permitted destination ports for this host. Each entry is a port number with an optional transport protocol (defaults to TCP).

StepCategory.title: Step Category
StepCategory.description: Platform-wide step taxonomy classification. Categorizes steps by their architectural role. Exactly four categories exist: 'action' (domain and API integrations), 'task' (atomic compute and script executors), 'workflow' (in-memory control-plane logic, including the parent-side subworkflow_call), and 'trigger' (event entry points, including the child-side subworkflow_trigger). Used for UI organization, routing decisions, and capability validation.

StepPaletteIcon.title: Step Palette Icon
StepPaletteIcon.description: Optional glyph shown beside the step in the React Flow visual builder's drag-and-drop palette drawer, interpreted as a PatternFly / Font Awesome icon name. Authored in the manifest and carried through compilation into the step-definition.json descriptor so the palette can render it without a frontend deployment. When omitted, the UI falls back to a per-category default icon.

CredentialSpecification.title: Credential Specification
CredentialSpecification.description: Step-level credential access specification. Credential references contain only UUIDs and presentation hints; the platform authorizes each request at dispatch time.

CredentialReference.title: Credential Reference
CredentialReference.description: Declarative, UUID-based reference to a platform-managed credential. Only the abstract credential_id is persisted in the manifest and compiled descriptor. Steps must never accept credential values as direct input strings. The execution plane resolves the reference and supplies the value out of band; injection, scrubbing, and persistence are execution-plane-owned.

credential_id.description: UUID of the credential stored in the platform's encrypted vault. This UUID is the sole secret abstraction: no plaintext secret, key, or token may appear in a step definition. Validated at workflow deployment time to ensure the credential exists and is accessible to the workflow owner.

credential_mount_type.description: Optional requested presentation hint for a resolved credential. 'env', 'file', 'tmpfs_file', and 'header' identify the form the step expects; the execution plane owns whether and how that hint is honored when constructing the runtime.

credential_mount_path.description: Optional requested target path for 'file' and 'tmpfs_file' credential presentation. The execution plane owns whether and how this path is made available. Required in the manifest when 'tmpfs_file' is selected; ignored for 'env' and 'header' presentations.

credential_header_name.description: HTTP header name requested when credential_mount_type='header' (e.g. 'Authorization', 'X-API-Key'). Ignored for all other presentation hints; the execution plane owns the runtime injection.

CredentialReferenceList.title: Credential Reference List
CredentialReferenceList.description: An ordered list of CredentialReference entries, allowing a single step to declare multiple simultaneous credentials (for example an SSH key, a cloud API token, and a vault password), each with its own mount type, mount path, and authorization scope.

InputParameter.title: Input Parameter Definition
InputParameter.description: A JSON Schema Draft-07 definition for one step input. Non-credential sensitive data (PII, business-sensitive fields) must set redact: true. Authentication credentials must NOT be declared as inputs at all -- use credentialSpecification.credential_references instead. The platform and execution plane use this flag to scrub flagged values from all observable paths.

redact.description: Marks a non-credential sensitive input (PII, business-sensitive data) for redaction. The value is still supplied to the step as a normal input, but the platform must keep it out of StandardOutputWrapper fields, workflow variables, error messages, stack traces, execution logs, and persisted state. Do not use this to pass authentication credentials; those must be platform-managed references.

StepRegistrationPolicy.title: Administrative Step Registration Policy
StepRegistrationPolicy.description: Syntara-owned registration settings. This object is an API payload component and must not be embedded in developer-authored manifest.yaml metadata.

sandbox_required.description: Whether the registered step must execute under the platform sandbox controls.

egress_policy.description: Administrative network egress mode applied to the selected worker pool.

worker_pool_selector.description: Affinity labels used to select an eligible worker pool. Pool provisioning may be automatic or assigned by operations.

StepInputs.title: Step Inputs
StepInputs.description: Draft-07 sub-schema describing a step's typed input properties, rendered as canvas form fields. Supports flat primitives, dynamic nested JSON/YAML objects (such as arbitrary key/value maps or host lists), oneOf/anyOf unions, and typed arrays. Each sensitive non-credential input property must explicitly set redact: true. 'properties' maps each input name to its JSON Schema; 'required' lists the mandatory input names.

properties.description: Map of input name to its JSON Schema definition. A value may itself be a nested object, a typed array, or a oneOf/anyOf union — not only a flat primitive.
